_deprecated.note: shipsTransiting, stranded, throughputPercent, transitsBaseline, insuranceMultiple, and status mix sources or are scalar projections of richer objects. status in particular switches producer (PortWatch, falling back to AIS) without saying which; use transits.*, insurance.*, dailyTransits.*, and verdict.status instead.

aisBaselineNote: transitsBaseline is withheld (null) until 72 hourly samples exist on the current tiled12-active30m basis. The basis reset on 2026-07-30, when the AIS scraper stopped taking one thinned request for the whole bounding box and began tiling it so each tile is saturated, stepping counts up roughly 3.4x on total; the median is withheld again until enough post-cutover samples build up, the same as it was for roughly 3 days after the first cutover on 2026-07-20. Samples on an earlier basis are not mixed in. It is an AIS concurrent-presence median, a different population from transits.baseline (IMF PortWatch daily crossings); do not divide one by the other.
aisFirstFixNote: aisConcurrentInZone counts only vessels whose movement was measured against an earlier position. aisFirstFixInZone counts vessels seen in the same window for the first time, which have nothing to compare against yet; they are in neither aisConcurrentInZone nor stranded.

aisGaps.countScope: count is a floor on hulls we stopped receiving, not a count of evasions. Read it against eligibleTankers, the screened tanker population, and against ambientDarkRate, the share of eligible non-tankers that went dark on the identical test. The two rates are close, so the evasion excess is not currently distinguishable from ambient dropout.
aisGaps.vesselsTrackedScope: vesselsTracked is a cumulative, all-time, all-type total (every vessel ever recorded anywhere in the wider AIS bbox). It is not the screened population behind count: that population is tankers only, with 50 or more sightings, last seen inside the core area.

capeSnapshot.note: transitsLast24h counts port arrivals only (departures are not published upstream), across ports on both sides of the strait. Not a Hormuz crossing count. Use transits.count for that. An arrival is a port-area entry event rather than a distinct hull: adjacent ports double count and an anchorage reposition can re-trigger one, so read arrivals24hTotal as an activity index. expectedTotal is a 30-day forward book (ships expected within the next 30 days), not a queue waiting now. This feed is retired: the upstream port pages moved these aggregates behind a subscription on 2026-08-28 and have published none since, so the figures are frozen at asOf. For live Hormuz-corridor port activity use /api/v1/ports; for live Cape traffic use the cape row in chokepoints above.

chokepointsNote: preCrisisBaselineMedian on every row is computed over one fixed window (baselineWindowStart to baselineWindowEnd) anchored to the Hormuz crisis. For hormuz that window is a genuine pre-crisis baseline. For bab-el-mandeb, suez and cape it is not: those routes were already carrying diverted Red Sea traffic within that window, so preCrisisBaselineMedian for those rows reads as wartime volume, not a peacetime figure.

bullets: Houthi forces have tightened their grip on Red Sea shipping lanes as Saudi Arabia shut its pipeline bypassing the Strait of Hormuz, per Dunya News and The Guardian.
Brent stood at $104.61, down 3.98% over 24 hours, as of 11:56 UTC; futures markets are closed and the figure is unchanged since pre-close settlement.
Iran and Gulf states are reported to be preparing talks on the Strait of Hormuz in Oman, per jordannews.jo, Caspian Post, Briefs Finance, and IndexBox; no major wire in this feed carries the report.
dailyBrief.summary: The Strait of Hormuz remains the axis of an acute transit and supply crisis. Dunya News and The Guardian report that Houthi forces have tightened their hold over strategic Red Sea positions, with The Guardian specifically reporting the capture of a strategic island on a vital oil shipping route. Saudi Arabia's closure of its East-West pipeline, reported by TradeWinds, removes what had been the primary alternative export corridor around the strait. The closure declaration itself remains contested: Iranian media declared the strait shut, while APPEC coverage carried by the outlet of record for that briefing notes tankers are transiting in darkness and oil flows persist. Neither claim should be read as settled. IMF PortWatch data for 2026-09-06, the most recently published day, recorded 6 transits against a pre-crisis baseline of 85 per day; PortWatch publishes weekly and a multi-day lag is normal. Separately, this site's tracking shows 442 vessels holding position away from berth as of 11:56 UTC. The Crisis Pressure composite sits in the extreme band, flat over 24 hours, with physical transit deviation as its top driver. The Escalation Forecast composite sits in the elevated band, also flat, with the Brent-WTI forward spread as its leading contributor; the two indices diverge, reflecting a gap between current operational strain and the forward risk signal. On the diplomatic side, jordannews.jo, Caspian Post, Briefs Finance, and IndexBox report Iran and Gulf states are preparing Oman talks, though no major wire in this feed carries the item. gCaptain reports tanker rates hit record highs following attacks on shipping.

dataHealthNote: dataHealth.events reflects producer health, not event recency, UNLESS no event has arrived for 12 hours, after which it falls back to the plain event-age gate, so a very quiet stretch beyond 12 hours can still read stale even with a healthy pipeline. Use dataHealth.events.verifiedAt for the newest event time.

premium.note: Machine-payable premium endpoints (x402, USDC on Base): full vessel manifest with sanctions cross-reference, single-vessel dossiers, a shadow-fleet risk screen of the vessels active on AIS in the Persian Gulf window, hourly history capped at one year with actual depth growing daily, bulk export, one-call snapshot, structured daily brief, real-time streaming, threshold-alert webhooks, and a Hormuz flag rollup. $0.01-$0.50 per request, no key or account. MCP connector at the mcp URL.

strandedNote: `stranded` counts every vessel not under way anywhere in the watch box, including ones at berth working cargo at regional ports such as Dubai and Abu Dhabi. `strandedOffshore` excludes vessels within 25km of a working port and is the narrower figure the site's own narrative uses.

transits.cadenceNote: Completed daily transits (IMF PortWatch crossing count). Not the same as aisConcurrentInZone, which is a snapshot of vessels moving inside the wider Persian Gulf watch box right now, not the Strait channel itself.
transits.freshestDayNote: The newest PortWatch row is always a Sunday, because IMF publishes weekly on Tuesday against data carrying a ~2-day lag. Sunday is the lowest-traffic weekday in this series, so the freshest print reads low against the day before it even in a normal week. Compare it with earlier Sundays, or with baselineMedian, rather than with previousNTotal.

verdict.long: War-risk insurance has priced commercial transit through the Strait of Hormuz beyond the reach of most operators.
